## Enable Prometheus

You will need to add `ENABLE_PROMETHEUS` environment variable as `true` in order to
enable Prometheus style metrics on the \<BASE_PATH\>/metrics route.
The OpenTelemetry and Prometheus packages it uses are part of the `all` extra, which the image
built from the repository's Dockerfile includes.

## Prometheus metrics

When enabled, MageML publishes metrics for the HTTP server (Tornado) as well as for
the Python runtime. The /metrics route will be updated on-demand to respond to scrape requests.

## Pipeline and block runs

Each scrape reads the project's runs from MageML's database, so runs that ran in the
scheduler, in workers or on other replicas count.

| Metric | Labels | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mage_pipeline_runs` | `pipeline`, `status` | Pipeline runs by status |
| `mage_block_runs` | `pipeline`, `block`, `status` | Block runs by status |
| `mage_pipeline_run_last_duration_seconds` | `pipeline` | Seconds the last completed run took |
| `mage_pipeline_run_last_success_timestamp_seconds` | `pipeline` | When the last completed run ended (Unix time) |

An alert on a pipeline that stopped succeeding:

```yaml
- alert: PipelineNotSucceeding
  expr: time() - mage_pipeline_run_last_success_timestamp_seconds{pipeline="orders"} > 2 * 3600
```

Exported services publish their own metrics on their `/metrics` route.
